entries.title: LQG metric dimension: parameter normalization
entries.statement: For each fixed gamma in (0,2), the gamma-Liouville quantum gravity metric D_h associated with a whole-plane Gaussian free field h has deterministic almost-sure Hausdorff dimension d_gamma. Its metric Weyl-scaling parameter is xi=gamma/d_gamma, and Q=2/gamma+gamma/2. Hence d_gamma=gamma/xi. These relations parametrize the unknown exponent; they do not evaluate it. The known Brownian-map anchor is d_sqrt(8/3)=4. Gamma=2 is outside this subcritical statement. Current openness on 2026-10-10 is UNKNOWN in this packet; a checked 2026-06-09 primary paper still reports the general value unknown.
assumptions: h is a whole-plane GFF with fixed additive constant
D_h is the gamma-LQG metric up to deterministic positive scale

entries.title: Draft correction: a prior LQG normalization identity is inconsistent
entries.statement: AUTHOR DRAFT, independent review pending w524. A related archived attempt D0049-A001 states d_gamma=2Q/xi. Under 0<gamma<2, D>0, xi=gamma/D and Q=2/gamma+gamma/2, direct substitution gives 2Q/xi=(1+4/gamma^2)D>D. The correct rearrangement is D=gamma/xi. At gamma^2=8/3 and D=4 the archived expression gives 10, whereas the corrected expression gives 4. This is a correction to an auxiliary statement; the original problem of determining the general metric dimension remains unresolved by this draft. The reviewer-only diff retains other archived statements as unaudited.
assumptions: only the stated normalization identity is audited

entries.title: Draft guard: KPZ and thick-point dimensions leave an unknown absolute scale
entries.statement: AUTHOR DRAFT, independent review pending w524. Assume 0<gamma<2, xi>0, Q=2/gamma+gamma/2, and 0<=x<=2. The maximum over alpha in [-2,2] of max(x-alpha^2/2,0)/(xi(Q-alpha)) is T(x)=(Q-sqrt(Q^2-2x))/xi. For x>0 the optimizer is uniquely alpha=Q-sqrt(Q^2-2x); for x=0 the expression is identically zero. At x=2, gamma/xi-(2-alpha^2/2)/(xi(Q-alpha))=(alpha-gamma)^2/(2xi(Q-alpha)). If xi=gamma/D for any positive numerical D, then T(x)/D=(Q-sqrt(Q^2-2x))/gamma and every KPZ equation x=xi*Q*T(x)-xi^2*T(x)^2/2 is satisfied. These equations alone do not identify D. This is a numerical nonidentifiability statement, not the existence of multiple LQG metrics. The metric KPZ theorem for a random Borel set requires independence from h; thick points use the dedicated theorem with an independent ambient set. No uncountable union or probability-one intersection is used here.
assumptions: numerical equations are distinguished from all metric axioms

entries.title: Draft guard: the thick-point critical corner depends on the approach path
entries.statement: AUTHOR DRAFT, independent review pending w524. For 0<gamma<2, xi>0 and -2<alpha<2, let Q=2/gamma+gamma/2 and F=(2-alpha^2/2)/(xi(Q-alpha)). Set delta=2-gamma and beta=2-alpha. Then xi*F=(2beta-beta^2/2)/(beta+delta^2/(2gamma)). As gamma and alpha approach 2 from below, if beta/delta^2 tends to finite k>=0, xi*F tends to 8k/(4k+1); if the ratio tends to infinity, the limit is 2. Every limit in [0,2] is possible, so there is no unique continuous extension at this corner. This is a deterministic algebraic boundary calculation, not a claim about the critical LQG metric or a coupling over gamma.
assumptions: the limit is of the numerical normalized spectrum xi*F

entries.title: Draft guard: the normalized KPZ inverse has sharp square-root stability
entries.statement: AUTHOR DRAFT, independent review pending w524. For 0<gamma<2, Q=2/gamma+gamma/2 and x in [0,2], define Y_gamma(x)=Q-sqrt(Q^2-2x). Its optimal Lipschitz constant at fixed gamma is 2gamma/(4-gamma^2), which is unbounded as gamma approaches 2. Uniformly in gamma and x,y in [0,2], |Y_gamma(x)-Y_gamma(y)|<=sqrt(2|x-y|). Across this family, the constant sqrt(2) and exponent 1/2 are sharp. Indeed, putting q=(4-gamma^2)/(2gamma), the endpoint deficit gamma-Y_gamma(2-epsilon) equals sqrt(q^2+2epsilon)-q. This inverse-map statement does not supply an absolute metric dimension or assert a critical metric theorem.
assumptions: Y is a numerical normalized inverse map

relations.rationale: The correction uses the primary normalization xi=gamma/d_gamma and its Brownian-map anchor.
Identifying D with a proposed absolute dimension uses xi=gamma/D and Q=2/gamma+gamma/2.
The maximum at x=2 bounds the normalized spectrum by gamma, giving the full range of corner limits.
The inverse endpoint is controlled by q_gamma^2, and the thick-point corner by delta^2; both degenerate quadratically near gamma=2.
The independent metric-normalization exponent is the missing quantity in the original exact-dimension target.
The prior constant-shift attempt already records xi*d=gamma and leaves xi unknown; this draft analyzes KPZ optimization and its critical corner.
